translation_notes: the seven self.graph.add(...) calls become four g{...} islands added with 'self.graph += g{...}', following the original control flow exactly (unconditional type triple, conditional info_class triple, description+date on one subject, conditional http Request block)
ns_rdf["type"] -> Turtle's 'a' in all three places

htbnode = BNode() is absorbed into an inline [ a ht:Request ; ht:requestURI {...} ] property list -- it was pure term-construction scaffolding used once as an object and then as a subject, exactly the case the notation is built for. The outer 'bnode' is KEPT as BNode() in Python: it is the return value and is used by up to four separate islands, and _:labels do not span islands.

Literal(full_msg) -> {full_msg} and Literal("%s" % context) -> {"%s" % context} (node() coercion of a str is Literal); Literal(datetime...isoformat(), datatype=ns_xsd["dateTime"]) -> {datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}^^xsd:dateTime, the glued-suffix form, which only exists inside an island

NEGATIVE FINDING: @prefix does not feed rdflib's namespace manager, so the six 'self.graph.bind("dcterms", ns_dc)' lines still need the Namespace objects. ns_dc/ns_ht and the ns_xsd/ns_distill/ns_rdfa imports are therefore kept AND six @prefix declarations added -- each namespace IRI is now written twice. The prefix names chosen are the ones the code itself binds (dcterms, pyrdfa, rdf, rdfa, ht, xsd), not the mechanical ns-dc/ns-ht/... derived from the Python variables.

the bind() calls are kept rather than dropped: the driver's isomorphism check does not depend on them, but pyRdfa serialises this processor graph, so they are observable in the real program (checked: both sides serialise with the same six prefixes)

context shim: 'from . import ns_xsd, ns_distill, ns_rdfa' -> local pyrdfa_shim.py copying those Namespace objects verbatim from pyRdfa/__init__.py. Two import lines missing from the extracted region were restored verbatim from the source file so it can run at all: 'from rdflib import Namespace' (used by ns_dc/ns_ht) and 'from rdflib import RDF as ns_rdf' (used by the region, and by the bind call). Identical for both sides.

driver freezes datetime.datetime.utcnow() for the whole run (both modules share the same datetime module object); without it the dcterms:date literal would differ between the two executions for reasons unrelated to the translation
